_comment: Useful phrases (Redemittel) by speech act: agreeing, disagreeing, doubting, comforting … Each set is a flashcard deck (/vocabulary/phrases/<id>) and a row under the phrases on /pronunciation. The key `de` holds the Spanish phrase that is practised (the key name is history, see docs/content-plan.md §1.4); `en` is the English meaning, with a short usage note where it helps. Every phrase has `variety`, and `es419` where Latin American usage differs. Phrase order matters: the beginner path refers to phrases as redemittel:<set>#<index>. Translations live in src/data/redemittel-i18n/<lang>.json, keyed by the Spanish phrase: machine drafts until a native speaker has read them (reviewed: false). Audio: scripts/generate-satz-audio.mjs → public/audio/redemittel/<slug>.mp3 (none yet for the Spanish phrases).

phrases.en: You're right. (To someone you call usted: Tiene razón.)
I completely agree.
Exactly!
I agree with you.
I think so too.

phrases.de: Eso es justo lo que pienso.
phrases.en: That's exactly what I think.
That sounds like a good idea.
OK, agreed. Vale is the everyday “OK” in Spain.

es419.note: Vale is typical of Spain. In Latin America: Bueno, de acuerdo, or regional forms such as Dale.

phrases.de: Yo lo veo de otra manera.
phrases.en: I see it differently.
I don't agree.

phrases.de: Eso no es del todo cierto.
phrases.en: That's not quite right.

phrases.de: Lo siento, pero no estoy de acuerdo.
phrases.en: I'm sorry, but I disagree. A polite way to say no.
I don't think that's true. (After no creo que comes the subjunctive: sea.)
I don't think so.
Yes, but … You agree a little, then add your point.
No way! (informal)
I'm not so sure about that.
Do you really think so?
I don't know, I'm not sure. (A woman says: segura.)
Is that really so?
I find that hard to believe.
Hmm, I have my doubts.
Are you sure? (To a woman: ¿Estás segura?)
I doubt it.
I'm so sorry.
Cheer up! Keep going!
It'll be all right.
Don't worry.

phrases.de: Aquí me tienes para lo que necesites.
phrases.en: I'm here for whatever you need.
It's not that bad. Careful: with a real problem it can sound dismissive.
You can do it!
Is there anything I can do for you?
My view is that …
I think that … The easiest way to give your opinion.
In my opinion, …
It seems to me that …

phrases.de: Para mí lo importante es que …
phrases.en: What matters to me is that … (Often followed by the subjunctive.)
To be honest, … (A woman says: sincera.)
That seems fine to me.
What do you think? (To someone you call usted: ¿Usted qué opina?)
Sorry? You didn't hear what someone said.
Could you say that again, please? (With tú: ¿Puedes repetir?)
Could you speak more slowly, please?
What does that mean?
Sorry, I didn't understand that.

es419.note: Many Latin American varieties (Mexico, for example) prefer the simple past here: no lo entendí.

phrases.en: How do you spell that?
Do you mean that …? You check that you have understood.
Could you give me an example?
Could you help me, please? A polite way to ask.
Have you got a minute? (With tú: ¿Tienes un momento?)
Could you pass me the salt, please?
Could I ask you a favour? (With tú: ¿Te puedo pedir un favor?)
Sorry to bother you. Say this before you interrupt someone.
Could you show me?
I need some help.
Would that be possible?
Sorry! For a small mistake, or when you bump into someone.
I'm really sorry.
I didn't mean it like that.
Sorry I'm late. (With usted: Perdone.)
That was my fault.

es419.note: Many Latin American varieties (Mexico, for example) prefer the simple past here: Fue culpa mía.

phrases.en: No problem. An answer to an apology: it's OK.
It doesn't matter. An answer to an apology: forget it.
It could happen to anyone. An answer to an apology.
Thank you very much!
Thanks, that's very kind of you.
Thank you so much for your help.
How thoughtful of you! For a small gift or a kind gesture.
You're welcome! An answer to thank you.
It was my pleasure. An answer to thank you.

es419.note: Many Latin American varieties (Mexico, for example) prefer the simple past here: Fue un placer.

phrases.en: Don't mention it. An answer to thank you.
I really appreciate it.
How about …? (¿Qué tal si vamos en metro?)
Shall we go out for a meal?
I suggest that we … (Followed by the subjunctive: Propongo que vayamos.)
Do you fancy going to the cinema?

es419.note: Te apetece is far more common in Spain. In Latin America you often hear ¿Quieres …? or ¿Tienes ganas de …?

phrases.en: Good idea, let's do that! A yes to a suggestion.

phrases.de: Lo siento, ese día no puedo.
phrases.en: Sorry, I can't make it that day. A no to a suggestion.
Maybe another time.
Is Saturday good for you?

es419.note: In Mexico and elsewhere ¿Te queda bien el sábado? is also common.

phrases.en: Congratulations! For an exam, a new job, a baby.

es419.note: Latin America more often says ¡Felicidades! or ¡Felicitaciones!

phrases.en: Happy birthday!
Good luck!
Good luck with your exam!
Get well soon! To someone who is ill.
Have a nice weekend! Said on Friday.
Merry Christmas!
I'm so happy for you!
Good morning! Used until lunchtime, which in Spain is often around two o'clock.
Nice to meet you. (A woman says: Encantada.)

es419.note: Mucho gusto is the more usual phrase in much of Latin America.

phrases.en: How are you? Answer: Bien, gracias. ¿Y tú?
Long time no see! (informal)
See you tomorrow!
Goodbye!
Take care! A friendly goodbye.
Have a good day!
In the picture I can see … The easiest way to start.

phrases.de: La foto muestra a una familia comiendo.
phrases.en: The picture shows a family having a meal. You say what it is about.
In the foreground you can see …
In the background there's a park.

phrases.de: En el centro hay una mesa.
phrases.en: In the middle there's a table.

phrases.de: A la izquierda hay una mujer joven sentada.
phrases.en: On the left there's a young woman sitting down.

phrases.de: En la esquina superior derecha hay una ventana.
phrases.en: In the top right-hand corner there's a window.

phrases.de: Seguramente la gente está de vacaciones.
phrases.en: The people are probably on holiday. A guess about the situation.

phrases.de: Creo que es una fiesta de cumpleaños.
phrases.en: I think it's a birthday party. A guess about the situation.
It looks as if everyone is happy.
The atmosphere is relaxed.

phrases.de: La foto me recuerda a mi infancia.
phrases.en: The picture reminds me of my childhood. You connect it with your own life.

phrases.de: La pelota está dentro de la caja.
phrases.en: The ball is in the box.

phrases.de: La pelota está encima de la caja.
phrases.en: The ball is on the box.

phrases.de: La pelota está debajo de la mesa.
phrases.en: The ball is under the table.

phrases.de: La lámpara cuelga sobre la mesa.
phrases.en: The lamp is hanging above the table. (Sobre can mean “on” or “above”.)

phrases.de: La pelota está al lado de la caja.
phrases.en: The ball is next to the box.

phrases.de: La pelota está delante de la caja.
phrases.en: The ball is in front of the box.

phrases.de: La pelota está detrás de la caja.
phrases.en: The ball is behind the box.

phrases.de: La pelota está entre las cajas.
phrases.en: The ball is between the boxes.

phrases.de: El cuadro está en la pared.
phrases.en: The picture is on the wall. (En covers “in”, “on” and “at”.)
